faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). A full-time agricultural science degree with crop-production plots and Student READY activities.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at GIET University?
faqs.answer: A dated August 2026 university report records a farmer exposure visit to Instructional Farm-I and research demonstration plots.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at GIET University?
faqs.answer: Instructional crop farms: The farm account describes undergraduate crop-production plots and research blocks. Bandhuguda orchard: The university identifies an orchard about one kilometre from the main campus.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for GIET University?
faqs.answer: Agriculture hostel allocation: The school states that five hostels serve agriculture students: three for boys and two for girls. Its description gives three to four students per room; individual allocations require confirmation. Dining and drinking water: The school describes a central mess, monitored food provision and hostel water coolers. Hostel recreation and emergency support: The facility account lists indoor games, gymnasiums and emergency ambulance provision, alongside internet access.

faqs.answer: GIET’s general scholarship page contains schemes with different programme scopes, including GIETEE/Board-of-Governance categories explicitly marked B.Tech-only. Agriculture applicants should ask which government reimbursement or institutional assistance actually applies to their course and entry year. Engineering award limits should not be transferred to agriculture.

Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.
